questions.q: In "What testing is for Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Count: tests passed, failed, defects by severity, defects found per hour.
Explain in plain words: testing is looking for the difference between what the app should do and what it does, before users find it.
Write 40 test cases in a table: id, goal, steps, expected result, actual result, pass or fail.
A mentor with testing experience reviews your coverage and tells you which risk area you missed.

questions.q: In "Kick-off circle Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Test design: equivalence groups (one value from each kind), boundaries (just inside and just outside a limit), and exploring with a time limit and a goal.
Add accessibility cases: large text, screen reader, contrast, tap size.
Peers ask three questions: who is it for, why you, what could go wrong.
Present to a review room: the app, the plan, the findings, the counts and your release recommendation.

questions.q: In "Write the test plan Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Reporting: a defect needs a clear title, exact steps, expected versus actual, evidence (screen capture), device and version, severity and who it affects.
Write each defect clearly. Rate severity: blocks use, serious, minor, cosmetic.
Scope: what you will test and what you will not. Environments: which phones, versions, screen sizes, network speeds.
Retest after any fix released by the owner and record the result.

questions.q: In "Test design, device coverage and reporting Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Reporting: a defect needs a clear title, exact steps, expected versus actual, evidence (screen capture), device and version, severity and who it affects.
List the 5 most important things a user must be able to do and what failure would cost them.
Write three lessons learned and one decision: ready to release, release with known issues, or hold.
Rewrite unclear defects and add tests for the missed risk area.

questions.q: In "Run the tests and find defects Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Explain in plain words: testing is looking for the difference between what the app should do and what it does, before users find it.
Spend one hour on free exploration with a goal (for example 'break the booking form') and log what you find.
Write the user: who uses it, on what phone, in what place (poor signal, one hand, bright sun).
Include the happy path, wrong inputs, empty fields, very long text, special characters, rotating the screen, interruptions (call, low battery), no network.

questions.q: In "Defect-review circle Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Peers try to reproduce three of your defects from the text only. Note any that fail.
Ask one real user, customer or reviewer for a short written note.
Of 10 fails, 3 are the same cause (long text breaks the layout) = 8 unique defects. Severity: 1 blocks use, 2 serious, 3 minor, 2 cosmetic.
Spend one hour on free exploration with a goal (for example 'break the booking form') and log what you find.
